primer.title: as, From/Into and TryFrom
body: `as` is a raw cast between primitive types. It never fails — it truncates or wraps instead: `300 as u8` is 44.
`From`/`Into` are for conversions that **cannot fail**; implementing `From<A> for B` gives you `a.into()` for free. `TryFrom`/`TryInto` return a `Result` for conversions that can fail.
There are no implicit numeric conversions, not even in arithmetic: `f64 / usize` does not compile.

exercises.prompt: This does not compile. What does the compiler object to?

options.text: E0277: line 3 divides an `f64` by a `usize`
options.rationale: Rust never converts numbers implicitly. `values.len() as f64` makes both sides `f64`.
`sum` can add up `&f64` items into an `f64`; the annotation on `total` selects that.
It would, with the cast. As written there is no `Div<usize>` for `f64`.

options.text: E0308: an array `[f64; 4]` cannot be passed as `&[f64]`
options.rationale: `&values` coerces from `&[f64; 4]` to a slice automatically.
`as` keeps the low 8 bits: 300 − 256 = 44. `try_from` checks the range instead, so 300 is an `Err` and 200 is `Ok`.
Integer-to-integer `as` truncates bits; it does not clamp. (Float-to-integer `as` is the one that saturates.)

options.text: It panics on line 4: 300 does not fit in a `u8`
options.rationale: `as` never panics. Overflow checks apply to arithmetic, not to casts.
Only exactly two fields with a numeric age return early with a custom `Person`. `b` fails `parse`, and `c` has a third field, so the third slot is not `None`: both fall through to John, 30.
The pattern demands `None` in the third slot. `"Mark,20,extra"` has `Some("extra")` there, so the `if let` does not match.
`parse` returns a `Result`; `if let Ok(age)` simply does not match an `Err`. Nothing unwraps.

options.text: It does not compile: `.into()` is not implemented for `&str`
options.rationale: Implementing `From<&str> for Person` provides `Into<Person> for &str` automatically.
